Rashi on Niddah 35a:11:1.english: Instances of "et" - [As it is written:] "And of him that has an issue, of his issue, whether male or female" (Leviticus 15:33).

Rashi on Niddah 35a:12:1.hebrew: זב חדא זובו תרתי לזכר - כלומר, עד כאן יש לו דין זכר שאינו מטמא באונס. מכאן ואילך, דהיינו שלישית, לנקבה כתיב, כלומר יש לו דין נקבה שמטמאה באונס, כדילפינן בפירקין (לקמן נדה דף לו:) מכי יזוב זוב, ואיהי נמי מייתא ליה לידי קרבן:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:12:1.english: "Zav" is one, "zovo" is two, "for a male" - That is to say, up to this point he has the legal status of a male, who does not become impure through circumstances beyond his control. From here on, that is, the third [sighting], it is written "to a female" — that is to say, he has the legal status of a female, who becomes impure through circumstances beyond her control, as we derive in our chapter (below, Niddah 36b) from "when [a discharge] issues"; and it [the third sighting] also brings him to [liability for] an offering.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:13:1.hebrew: ברביעית - אז אקשיה רחמנא לנקבה, דאפילו באונס. ולא לענין טומאה, דהא מכי חזיא תרתי איטמי ליה; ולקרבן נמי לא, דמשלשה איחייב ליה; אלא לסתירה, כגון דפסק והתחיל לספור שבעה נקיים, וראה ראייה רביעית — אפילו באונס סותר:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:13:1.english: On the fourth [sighting] - Then the Merciful One compared him to a female, such that [it counts] even due to circumstances beyond his control. And [this is] not with regard to ritual impurity, for once he has seen two [sightings], he has become ritually impure; and also not with regard to a sacrifice, for from three [sightings] he has become obligated in it; rather, with regard to nullification [of clean days]: such as where [his discharge] ceased and he began to count seven clean days, and he saw a fourth sighting — even [if it occurred] due to circumstances beyond his control, it nullifies [his count].

Rashi on Niddah 35a:14:1.hebrew: והלא זב בכלל בעל קרי היה - כדמפרש לקמיה ואזיל, דאיתקוש לשכבת זרע:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:14:1.english: Was not a zav included in [the category of] one who experienced a seminal emission - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain below, that it was juxtaposed with seminal emission.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:14:2.english: And why was he taken out - In the passage of zavim, to be written on his own.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:14:3.english: To be lenient with him, that he does not become impure due to circumstances beyond his control - For a seminal emission imparts impurity [even] due to circumstances beyond one's control.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:1:1.hebrew: לאחרים גורם טומאה - כלומר, טיפה זו גורמת לבעלה שמטמא במשא, כדכתיב (ויקרא טו) וכל אשר יהיה תחתיו, ואוקמינן בעליונו של זב — היא עצמה לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:1:1.english: It causes impurity for others - That is to say, this drop causes its possessor [the zav] to impart impurity through carrying, as it is written (Leviticus 15): "And whatever was under him," and we established [this verse as referring to] the upper burden of a zav; is it not all the more so that [the drop] itself [imparts impurity through carrying]?

Rashi on Niddah 35a:1:2.hebrew: אלא בזב מצורע - איצטריך, דלא אתי בקל וחומר, דלא גרמה לו טומאה, שהרי מחמת נגעו היה מטמא במשא ואפילו באהל:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:1:2.english: Rather, in [the case of] a zav who is a leper - [A verse] was necessary, as it could not be derived through an a fortiori inference, since [the discharge] did not cause him impurity, for on account of his affliction he was [already] imparting impurity through carrying, and even in a tent.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:2:1.hebrew: ומדאיצטריך קרא לרבויי לשניה ש"מ - בראשונה דלאו מעיין הוא, דאי מעיין הוא — ראשונה מטמאה, שניה לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:2:1.english: And from the fact that a verse was needed to include the second, conclude from it - [Regarding] the first [sighting], that it is not a source; for if it were a source, the first [sighting] would impart impurity, [and as for] the second, is it not all the more so?!

Rashi on Niddah 35a:3:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך בזב גרידא - דאי במצורע, לא איצטריך קרא לרבויי, דאפילו ראשונה מטמא משום מעיין:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:3:1.english: Actually, I could say to you [that it is] regarding a mere zav - For if [it were speaking] of a leper, a verse would not be needed to include [him], since even [his] first [sighting] imparts impurity as a source.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:3:2.hebrew: ודקאמרת כו' שעיר המשתלח יוכיח שגורם טומאה - למשלחו, כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ו) והמשלח את השעיר וגו', והוא עצמו טהור, שאין בהמה מטמאה מחיים:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:3:2.english: And that which you said, etc., the scapegoat will prove, for it causes impurity - To its dispatcher, as it is written (Leviticus 16:26): "And he who sends the goat, etc.," and [the goat] itself is pure, for an animal does not become impure while alive.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:4:1.english: Why should it be a dilemma to him - [This refers] to Rav Yosef.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:4:2.hebrew: הא איהו אמר כו' בין קטן בין גדול - לזיבה, ולא איצטריך והזב את זובו לזכר לרבות קטן, דהא מזאת תורת הזב נפקא, ואייתר לזכר לרבות מצורע:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:4:2.english: Was it not he who said, etc., whether a minor or an adult - [This is] with regard to zivah, and it was not necessary [for the verse] "and of him that has an issue of his issue, whether it be a male" to include a minor, for this is derived from "This is the law of the zav," and "whether it be a male" remains superfluous, to include a leper.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:5:1.hebrew: ואיתקש מצורע לזב גמור - בעל שתי ראיות, דהא בהאי קרא דהיקשא דמצורע תרתי כתיבי: "והזב את זובו" - הרי שתים, וכתיב ביה "לזכר" לרבות מצורע, כדין זב גמור: מה זב גמור זובו מטמא במשא, אף מצורע זובו מטמא במשא, ואפילו ראשונה. דבשלמא אי מפיק ליה האי "לזכר" לזב קטן, ויליף מצורע זכר ממצורעת נקבה, איכא למבעי: ראייה ראשונה מהו? מי הוי מתעגל ויוצא ומתרבי עם שאר מעיינות, או לאו? דבנקבה ליכא זוב לובן למילפיה מהיקשא דזב גמור אי לאו מעיין הוי. אבל השתא דמצורע זכר איתקש לזב גמור, לא צריך תו למבעי: ואית דמפרשי בעיא דרב יוסף הכי: ראייה ראשונה של מצורע מהו שתטמא במשא? בזב גרידא לא תבעי לך, דודאי מטמא, כדאמר לקמן: לימד על הזוב שהוא טמא, ומוקמינן בדם הנדה דקרא למשא אתא. כי תבעי לך - במצורע, דאיכא למימר: בזב גרידא הוא דמטמא משום דגורמת לו טומאה, אבל במצורע כבר טמא הוא ואינה גורמת לו טומאה, לא מטמיא הטיפה אי לא אמרינן מעיין הוא כרוקו או מימי רגליו; מאי, מעיין הוא או לא? לימד על הזוב, ומוקמינן לה בראייה ראשונה, והכי משמע: כי יהיה זב מבשרו - אותו הזב טמא. לאחרים? לבעלה! ומדאיצטריך לרבויי לראייה ראשונה, ש"מ לאו מעיין הוא. ושיבוש הוא מפני כמה תשובות: חדא, דקא פשיט ליה מקום זיבה לאו מעיין הוא, והא למשא רבייה קרא, כדאמר בדם הנדה, מה לי מעיין ומה לי לאו מעיין? ועוד, מי איכא לאוקמי להאי קרא בראייה ראשונה? והא מהכא נפקא לן בכל דוכתי: מנה הכתוב שתים וקראו טמא! ועוד, מי איכא למימר בראייה ראשונה בזב גרידא לאחרים גורם טומאת משא? הא זב בעל ראייה אחת אינו אלא כרואה קרי, כדאמר בכמה מקומות: שתים לטומאת זיבה ושלש לקרבן! ועוד, ראייה ראשונה הא אקשיה לעיל לקרי, וקרי לא מטמא במשא! ומשום שכתוב בספרים: מדאיצטריך קרא בראייה ראשונה, מפרשי ליה הכי. ולאו מילתא היא, דהאי "בראייה ראשונה" פירוש היה בספרים ולקמיה קאי, והכי קאמר: מדאיצטריך קרא לרבויי לשניה, ש"מ ראשונה מקום זיבה לאו מעיין הוא. וה"ג בשלהי שמעתתא: מה זב גמור מטמא זובו במשא אף מצורע כו', אלמא זב גמור הוא דמטמא טיפת זובו במשא, אבל זב בעל ראייה אחת לא:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:5:1.english: And the leper is equated to a full-fledged zav - [Meaning,] one who has had two sightings. For in this verse containing the analogy to the leper, two [sightings] are written: "And one who has an issue [hazav] of his issue [et zovo]" (Leviticus 15:33) — behold, two! And it is written in it: "whether it be a male" [lazakhar], to include a leper, [treating him] according to the law of a full-fledged zav: Just as [with] a full-fledged zav, his discharge imparts impurity through carrying, so too [with] a leper, his discharge imparts impurity through carrying, and even on the first [sighting]. For granted, if he [Rav Yosef] had applied this [word] "whether it be a male" to a minor zav, and derived a male leper from a female leper, there would be room to inquire: Regarding a first sighting, what is the law? Does it form and discharge and is it included along with the other bodily secretions, or not? For in a female there is no white discharge from which to derive it via an analogy to a full-fledged zav if it is not a [natural] source. But now that a male leper is equated to a full-fledged zav, he no longer needs to inquire. And there are those who explain Rav Yosef's dilemma as follows: With regard to a first sighting of a leper, what is the law as to whether it imparts impurity through carrying? In [the case of] just a zav, you should not have a dilemma, for it certainly imparts impurity, as [the Gemara] says later: "It taught regarding the discharge that it is impure," and we establish in [the chapter] Dam HaNiddah that the verse comes to [teach impurity transmitted through] carrying. Where your dilemma arises is with regard to a leper. For one could say: It is only in [the case of] just a zav that it imparts impurity, because it causes impurity to him; but in the case of a leper, he is already impure, and it does not cause impurity to him; [therefore,] the drop should not impart impurity unless we say that it is a source like his saliva or his urine. What, then: is it a source or not? "It taught regarding the discharge," and we establish it as referring to a first sighting. And this is what it means: "When any man has an issue out of his flesh" — that discharge is impure. To others? To its owner! And from the fact that it was necessary to include a first sighting, conclude from it that it is not a source. And this is an error, on account of several refutations: First, that he resolves it [by saying that] the place of zivah is not a source — but behold, the verse included it for carrying, as [the Gemara] says in Dam HaNiddah; what does it matter to me whether it is a source or whether it is not a source? Furthermore, can one establish this verse as referring to a first sighting? But behold, from here we derive in all places: "The verse counted two [sightings] and called him impure"! Furthermore, can one say regarding a first sighting in [the case of] just a zav that it causes the impurity of carrying to others? Behold, a zav who experienced one sighting is merely like one who experienced a seminal emission, as [the Gemara] says in several places: "Two [sightings are required] for the impurity of zivah, and three for an offering"! Furthermore, a first sighting was equated above to a seminal emission, and semen does not impart impurity through carrying! And because it is written in [some] books: "From the fact that the verse was necessary [to include] in a first sighting," they explain it this way. But this is not correct, for this [phrase] "in a first sighting" was an explanatory gloss in the books, and it applies to what follows; and this is what it means: From the fact that the verse was necessary to include the second [sighting], conclude from it that regarding the first [sighting], the place of zivah is not a source. And this is the textual reading at the conclusion of the sugya: "Just as a full-fledged zav, his discharge imparts impurity through carrying, so too a leper, etc." — which proves that it is [only] a full-fledged zav whose drop of discharge imparts impurity through carrying, but a zav who experienced one sighting does not.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:6:1.hebrew: מטמא באונס - אותה טומאה קלה האמורה בה, מגע וטומאת ערב בקרי, ולהצטרף לשניה לטמא כזב גמור. והא דכתיב מבשרו ולא מחמת אונסו, על כרחך אראייה שניה דכתיב בתרה קאי, ולא אראשונה, דהא איתקש לשכבת זרע, ושכבת זרע כל עצמו מחמת אונס חימום בא:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:6:1.english: Imparts impurity due to circumstances beyond one's control - [It imparts] that light impurity stated regarding it — contact and evening impurity, as with a seminal emission — and [serves] to combine with a second [sighting] to render [him] impure as a full zav. And that which is written: "Out of his flesh" — [from which it is derived:] "and not due to circumstances beyond his control" — perforce applies to the second sighting, which is written after it, and not to the first [sighting]; for [the first sighting] is compared to a seminal emission, and a seminal emission, by its very nature, comes about through the compulsion of [bodily] heat.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:1.hebrew: בודקין אותו - בשבעה דרכים: במאכל, במשתה, בקפיצה ובמשאוי כו':
Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:1.english: One examines him - In seven ways: through food, through drink, through jumping, and through [carrying] a load, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:2.hebrew: מאי לאו לטומאה - דאי באונס הוא, הוי טהור לגמרי:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:2.english: What, is it not for impurity - For if it was due to circumstances beyond his control, he would be completely pure.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:3.hebrew: לא לקרבן - דאי קמייתא באונס, לא מצטרפא לשלש לחייבו קרבן:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:7:3.english: No, for an offering - For if the first [sighting] was due to circumstances beyond his control, it does not combine to [make] three to obligate him to bring an offering.

Rashi on Niddah 35a:8:1.hebrew: אילימא לקרבן אבל לטומאה - האמורה בו, דהיינו טומאה חמורה, לא בעי בדיקה:
Rashi on Niddah 35a:8:1.english: If we say for an offering, but for ritual impurity - [As for the ritual impurity] stated regarding him, that is, severe impurity, does he not require an examination?

Rashi on Niddah 35a:8:2.english: Read here: "Out of his flesh," and not due to circumstances beyond his control - And this "out of his flesh" is written in the verse of two sightings.

Tosafot on Niddah 35a:10:1.hebrew: מכלל דתנא קמא לטומאה - לאו מן הלשון מדקדק: מדאצטריך ר' אליעזר להזכיר קרבן, מכלל דת"ק איירי לטומאה, דא"כ לא הוה משני מידי. אלא הכי דייק: מכלל דתנא קמא לא מצריך בדיקה משום קרבן אלא משום טומאה; דאי משום קרבן, הוה ליה לאצרוכי נמי בדיקה בשלישי כרבי אליעזר. וקשה, דהא בלאו מילתיה דרבי אליעזר הוה מצי למפרך, מדקתני במס' זבים (פרק ב' מ"ב) בהדיא במילתיה דרבנן גופייהו: בשלישי אין בודקין אותו. ושמא מייתי מרבי אליעזר, משום דבעי לפרושי במאי פליגי:
Tosafot on Niddah 35a:10:1.english: By inference, the first Tanna [is referring] to ritual impurity - [The Gemara] does not infer from the wording: "Since Rabbi Eliezer needed to mention an offering, by inference the first Tanna is dealing with ritual impurity" — for if so, it would not have answered anything. Rather, this is what it infers: By inference, the first Tanna does not require examination on account of an offering, but rather on account of ritual impurity; for if [it were] on account of an offering, he should have required examination on the third [discharge] as well, like Rabbi Eliezer. And [this is] difficult, for even without the statement of Rabbi Eliezer, [the Gemara] could have objected from that which is taught in Tractate Zavim (Chapter 2, Mishnah 2) explicitly in the statement of the Rabbis themselves: "On the third, they do not examine him." And perhaps [the Gemara] cites [the statement of] Rabbi Eliezer because it wanted to explain what they disagree about.

Tosafot on Niddah 35a:1:1.hebrew: לאחרים גורם טומאה - פירש רש"י: לזב עצמו גורם טומאת משא, כדכתיב: "וכל אשר יהיה תחתיו", ואוקמינן ליה בעליונו של זב. ואין נראה, דעליונו של זב אינו קרוי משא, ואינו מטמא אלא אוכלין ומשקין. ועוד, דבזוב כי האי גוונא לא אשכחן, אלא כשהטיפה בכף מאזנים וכרעה לכף שניה. לכן נראה לפרש: לזב עצמו גורם טומאת משא — שהנושא הזב טמא, הנושא הזוב לא כל שכן דטמא? ובשאר טומאות דלאו משא, כגון משכב ומושב, אין לפרש — דהא למצורע נמי גורם טומאה, דאילו מצורע גרידא אינו עושה משכב ומושב אלא לטמא אוכלין ומשקין, כדפרישית בפרק אלו דברים (פסחים סו.), ואם זב הוא, מטמא משכבו אדם ובגדים:
Tosafot on Niddah 35a:1:1.english: It causes impurity to others - Rashi explained: It causes the impurity of carrying to the zav himself, as it is written: “And whatever is under him” (Leviticus 15:10), and we established this [as referring to] that which is above a zav (elyono shel zav). But this does not appear [correct], for that which is above a zav is not called carrying (massa), and it only defiles food and drink. Furthermore, in the case of zov, such a case is not found except when the drop was on one pan of a balance and caused the second pan to tilt. Therefore, it seems [proper] to explain: It causes the impurity of carrying to the zav himself — [meaning,] that one who carries the zav is ritually impure; is not one who carries the zov all the more so ritually impure? And it cannot be explained [as referring] to other impurities that are not carrying, such as bedding and seating (mishkav u-moshav), for behold, [if so,] it would also cause impurity for a leper (metzora) — as a mere metzora makes bedding and seating [impure] only to defile food and drink, as I explained in chapter Elu Devarim (Pesachim 66a), whereas if he is a zav, his bedding defiles a person and garments.

Tosafot on Niddah 35a:3:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך בזב גרידא - תימה, דמכל מקום תפשוט דלאו מעיין הוא: דאי מעיין הוא, למה לי קרא לטמא בזוב? דהא מיד שראה משהו של ראייה שניה, מיד נעשה זב — למ"ד זוב מטמא במשהו, דלא בעי כחתימת פי האמה — ומשהו שני לטמא כדין מעיין, דאי אפשר לטיפה שלא תתחלק שני משהויין! ושמא, כמו שמשהו ראשון שבו נעשה זב אינו מטמא במשא, הוא הדין כל מה שנקרא ראייה אחת — דהיינו כמו גריון לשילה (זבים פ"א מ"ה) — דלא מטמא במשא; אע"ג דרוקו ומימי רגליו טמאין מיד אחר ראיית זוב משהו ראשון:
Tosafot on Niddah 35a:3:1.english: Actually, I could say to you [that the verse refers] to just a zav - This is difficult, for in any case, let [the Gemara] resolve that [the place of zivah] is not a source (ma'ayan): For if it were a source, why do I need a verse to impart impurity to zov [through carrying]? For as soon as he saw a minute amount (mashehu) of the second sighting, he immediately became a zav — according to the one who holds that zov imparts impurity with a minute amount, who does not require [an emission equal to] the sealing of the orifice of the member — and the second minute amount would impart impurity according to the law of a source, as it is impossible for a drop not to be divided into two minute amounts! And perhaps just as the first minute amount through which he becomes a zav does not impart impurity through carrying, the same applies to whatever is called "one sighting" — that is, [an emission lasting] like [the time from] Gariyon to Shiloh (Zavim 1:5) — that it does not impart impurity through carrying, even though his saliva and his urine are impure immediately after the sighting of the first minute amount of zov.

Tosafot on Niddah 35a:5:1.hebrew: אף ראייה ראשונה של מצורע מטמאה במשא - תימה: אם כן, לעיל מנליה לאוקומי קרא בדם טהרה של מצורעת? הא איצטריך קרא לכדהכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 35a:5:1.english: Even the first sighting of a leper imparts impurity through carrying - [This is] puzzling: If so, earlier, from where does [the Gemara] have [the basis] to establish the verse as referring to the blood of purity (dam tohorah) of a female leper? Behold, the verse is needed for [the teaching] here!

Tosafot on Niddah 35a:7:1.hebrew: מאי לאו לטומאה - וא"ת: מאי קושיא? דילמא הא דאמר רב הונא מטמא באונס, היינו טומאת ערב כבעל קרי, והכא מיירי להצטרף לשניה לטמא טומאה חמורה לעשותו זב, והוי השתא שפיר רישא דומיא דסיפא. וי"ל: מדלא נקט הרואה ראייה אחת של זיבה, אלא נקט ראייה ראשונה של זב, משמע דאיירי באותו שראה שתי ראיות והראשונה היתה באונס, דזב אינו קרוי עד שיראה שתי ראיות; ויליף מהיקשא דזאת תורת דאיירי בזב גמור, ומקיש ראשונה של השתים לשכבת זרע:
Tosafot on Niddah 35a:7:1.english: What, is it not for ritual impurity - And if you say: What is the difficulty? Perhaps that which Rav Huna said, "[The first sighting] imparts impurity [even] due to circumstances beyond his control," refers to evening impurity, like [that of] a ba'al keri [one who had a seminal emission], whereas here [in the mishna] it is dealing with [whether it] combines with the second to impart severe impurity, [namely] to render him a zav — and the first clause would then be nicely analogous to the latter clause! And one can say: Since [Rav Huna] did not state, "One who sees a single sighting of zivah," but rather stated, "The first sighting of a zav," this implies that it deals with one who saw two sightings and the first occurred due to circumstances beyond his control — for one is not called a zav until he sees two sightings; and he derives [this] from the juxtaposition of "This is the law of the zav" (Leviticus 15:32), which deals with a full-fledged zav, and [the verse] compares the first of the two [sightings] to a seminal emission.
